page: Vultr voc-m-2c-16gb-400s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute instance built on the x86_64 architecture. The server provides 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from a single AMD EPYC physical core running at 2.0 GHz, supporting two threads per core. Cache sizing includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache. Memory capacity is allocated at 16.0 GB total, yielding an 8:1 RAM-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. The hardware profile includes 400 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and one complimentary public IPv4 address, without an accelerator GPU.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-thread performance alongside lower aggregate throughput due to the low core count. The instance achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 2115.0 and a stress-ng single-core rating of 2934.07, both placing in the top 25%. Geekbench text processing also scores in the top tier at 2525.0. Conversely, multi-threaded metrics such as the Geekbench multi-core score (3785.0), PassMark CPU score (5470.65), and stress-ng multi-core test (5824.37) rank in the bottom 25%. Memory subsystem throughput is average across larger transfers, recording 74.28 GB/sec read and 53.91 GB/sec write on 256 MB blocks.

The 8:1 memory configuration combined with bundled 400 GB NVMe local storage provides solid cost efficiency for memory-centric, low-concurrency deployments. The primary architectural tradeoff is limited parallel compute; workloads requiring extensive multi-core throughput, high static web concurrency (2.26 GB/sec throughput), or large-scale database operations are constrained by the dual-vCPU count. The configuration is appropriate for memory-resident caching layers, staging environments, single-threaded processing pipelines, and light database instances needing high per-thread execution speed.

The instance includes 400 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and excludes GPU accelerators. Single-threaded benchmarks are strong, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2115.0 and stress-ng single-core score of 2934.07 placing in the top 25%. However, multi-core capacity is constrained by the two-vCPU ceiling, placing aggregate Geekbench multi-core (3785.0) and PassMark CPU metrics in the bottom 25%. Uncached 256 MB memory bandwidth tests reach 74.28 GB/sec read and 53.91 GB/sec write. With an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio and built-in NVMe storage, it offers cost-efficient headroom for memory-heavy, low-concurrency services, single-threaded workers, and small memory-resident databases.
